title: How UPI Changed Money in India
description:
In 2016 India switched on a payments system that now moves more real-time transactions than anywhere else on Earth. This is how UPI actually works.

#upi #india #fintech #economy #shorts

scenes.text: In 2016 India switched on a payments system that almost nobody outside the country had heard of. Today it moves more real-time transactions than anywhere else on Earth.
It is called UPI, the Unified Payments Interface. It was built by the National Payments Corporation of India, a non-profit created by the country's own banks.
The idea was simple. Instead of moving money bank to bank, UPI gives every account one address, so a transfer becomes a single instruction instead of three.
It costs the user nothing, works across every bank, and settles in seconds. On card networks merchants pay a fee. On UPI, that fee largely disappeared.
That is why it scaled. Not because the technology was clever on its own, but because it was cheap, open, and pushed every bank onto the same rails.
